title: Fetching in an Effect: ignore stale answers

slides.text: Alice clicked, Bob shown… then Alice? 🏁
slides.say: You switch from Alice to Bob. Alice’s request was slow, so it arrives last, and the screen shows the wrong person.

slides.text: Responses can arrive in a different order than the requests were sent.
slides.say: That’s a race condition. Network answers can come back in any order.
Fix it with an ignore flag. It starts as false. Cleanup sets it to true. Only a request whose flag is still false may set state.

slides.text: When userId changes, the old Effect’s cleanup runs, so Alice’s late answer is ignored.
slides.say: When the user I D changes, cleanup runs for Alice’s Effect. Her answer can still arrive, but it gets ignored.

slides.text: Using a framework? Its built-in data fetching is usually better.
slides.say: One more tip: if you use a framework, its built-in data fetching is usually a better choice than fetching in Effects.
